title: hello-research — an autonomous research agent that must cite (target: research)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “An agent that researches one sub-question at a time using local source documents.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec — a research contract

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “target: research” — plan, branch, cite, report. No REPL in this one.

beats.label: Add the agent and its job
beats.cue: Haiku, and the rule that shapes everything after it: one sub-question at a time.

beats.label: Spell out the four steps
beats.cue: Load every source, pick at most 2 verbatim snippets, CiteFact each one, then answer.

beats.label: Give it the goal
beats.cue: The question ships in the spec: what shapes exist, grouped shipped versus planned.

beats.label: Cap the run
beats.cue: Three branches, four minutes. The budget is a spec field, not a hope.

beats.label: Fence the filesystem
beats.cue: Its entire world is ./sources — harness-relative, so a copy works anywhere.

beats.label: Open the corpus it's fenced to
beats.cue: Three markdown files. This is the one with the shipped-versus-planned split.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: Goal, branching factor and the allowed file roots all lower into the IR.

verify.note: prints the IR for target research (33 lines)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: One .ts file — the other is the generated README — and it holds the whole loop: decompose the goal, run a branch each, write a cited report.

beats.label: Try crewhaus run
beats.cue: “run supports target cli or browser” — research is compile-only. The bundle is the runtime.

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1: `crewhaus run` supports cli|browser; other shapes are compile-only

beats.label: Boot the bundle
beats.cue: [needs-key] It writes its own sub-questions first, then researches them one branch at a time.

verify.note: plan → branch per sub-question → report; needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Read the report it wrote
beats.cue: [needs-key] No merge step, no executive summary: the goal as the title, one section per sub-question, then the numbered Citations list — each number a file:// URI and the snippet a branch quoted from it.

verify.note: newest report only — a bare `*/report.md` glob cats every earlier run on a re-take. report-writer's renderMarkdown emits exactly `# <goal>`, `## <sub-question>` + that branch's answer, then `## Citations`; there is no synthesis pass, and the Citations block appears only if some branch actually called CiteFact

groups.title: One more thing · the goal is a flag

beats.label: Point it at a different question
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same bundle, same fenced corpus — a new goal and a single branch.
beats.command: bun live/dist/agent.ts --goal "Which target shapes are still planned, and what ships each one?" --branching 1

verify.note: --goal and --branching override the spec defaults at launch

beats.label: List the runs on disk
beats.cue: [needs-key] One directory per run: report.md, report.json, and the state.json --resume reads.

verify.note: the directory only exists after a needs-key run
